488	def normalize_csv(source, schema, duplicate_by=None, filter_eq=None):
489	    columns, sources, defaults, allowed, markers, ranges, lte_fields = _prepare_schema(schema)
490	    names = [column["name"] for column in columns]
491	    column_index = {name: index for index, name in enumerate(names)}
492	    duplicate_fields = _prepare_duplicate_by(duplicate_by, names)
493	    filter_condition = _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns)
494	    records, errors = [], []
495	    # strict=True turns the two quote-syntax problems that a lenient reader
496	    # silently folds into the data into csv.Error: a quoted field still open
497	    # at EOF and any character other than comma/newline/EOF right after a
498	    # closing quote (a space or tab included). A doubled "" inside a quoted
499	    # field still decodes to one literal double quote, and a double quote
500	    # inside an unquoted field stays an ordinary character.
501	    with Path(source).open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as handle:
502	        reader = csv.reader(handle, strict=True)
503	        # reader.line_num is the physical line where the row just read ends;
504	        # LF, CRLF (counted once) and a lone CR all terminate a line. A
505	        # record's starting physical line is one past the end of the
506	        # preceding row, so skipped empty lines and newlines inside quoted
507	        # fields shift it down. When the strict reader reports a syntax
508	        # error the failing record starts on previous_end + 1, even though
509	        # the problem is only detected at a later physical line or at EOF.
510	        previous_end = 0
511	        header = None
512	        try:
513	            for cells in reader:
514	                start_line = previous_end + 1
515	                previous_end = reader.line_num
516	                if header is None:
517	                    header = cells
518	                    if header != sources:
519	                        raise ValueError(
520	                            "CSV header must match schema column sources and order exactly")
521	                    continue
522	                if not cells:
523	                    # An ordinary empty physical line: skipped as a record but it
524	                    # still occupies a physical line number (tracked above).
525	                    continue
526	                record = {}
527	                if len(cells) != len(sources):
528	                    row_errors = ["wrong number of cells"]
529	                else:
530	                    # One error slot per column keeps per-field errors and
531	                    # the lte_field relation error attributed to a column in
532	                    # schema column order, even when the relation points
533	                    # backward at an earlier column.
534	                    slots = [[] for _ in columns]
535	                    field_error_names = set()
536	                    for index, (column, value) in enumerate(zip(columns, cells)):
537	                        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
538	                        value = value.strip()
539	                        if value in markers.get(name, ()):
540	                            # A declared missing marker matches the trimmed
541	                            # cell exactly (case-sensitive) before any type
542	                            # conversion and then follows the empty-value
543	                            # flow: default, required error or null.
544	                            value = ""
545	                        try:
546	                            if not value:
547	                                if name in defaults:
548	                                    converted = defaults[name]
549	                                elif column.get("required", False):
550	                                    raise ValueError("required value is empty")
551	                                else:
552	                                    converted = None
553	                            elif kind == "integer":
554	                                converted = int(value)
555	                            elif kind == "boolean":
556	                                if value.casefold() not in ("true", "false"):
557	                                    raise ValueError("boolean must be true or false")
558	                                converted = value.casefold() == "true"
559	                            else:
560	                                converted = value
561	                        except ValueError as exc:
562	                            slots[index].append(f"{name}: {exc}")
563	                            field_error_names.add(name)
564	                            continue
565	                        enum_error = _enum_field_error(name, converted, allowed)
566	                        if enum_error is not None:
567	                            slots[index].append(enum_error)
568	                            field_error_names.add(name)
569	                            continue
570	                        range_error = _range_field_error(name, converted, ranges)
571	                        if range_error is not None:
572	                            slots[index].append(range_error)
573	                            field_error_names.add(name)
574	                        else:
575	                            record[name] = converted

577	                            record, field_error_names, lte_fields):
578	                        slots[column_index[name]].append(message)

582	                else:

585	            raise _csv_parse_error(

587	        if header is None:

592	def _convert_jsonl_value(column, value, defaults, markers):
593	    """Convert one decoded JSON value. Returns (converted, error_message)."""
594	    name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]

596	        value = value.strip()

599	            # booleans, arrays and objects never do); a hit follows the
600	            # empty-value flow before any type conversion.
601	            value = ""
602	    if value is None or value == "":
603	        if name in defaults:
604	            return defaults[name], None
605	        if column.get("required", False):
606	            return None, f"{name}: required value is empty"
607	        return None, None
608	    if kind == "string":
609	        if not isinstance(value, str):
610	            return None, f"{name}: expected string"
611	        return value, None
612	    if kind == "integer":
613	        if isinstance(value, bool):
614	            return None, f"{name}: expected integer"
615	        if isinstance(value, int):
616	            return value, None
617	        if isinstance(value, str):
618	            try:
619	                return int(value), None
620	            except ValueError:
621	                pass
622	        return None, f"{name}: expected integer"
623	    if isinstance(value, bool):
624	        return value, None
625	    if isinstance(value, str):
626	        folded = value.casefold()
627	        if folded in ("true", "false"):
628	            return folded == "true", None
629	    return None, f"{name}: boolean must be true or false"

632	def normalize_jsonl(source, schema, duplicate_by=None, filter_eq=None):
633	    columns, sources, defaults, allowed, markers, ranges, lte_fields = _prepare_schema(schema)
634	    names = [column["name"] for column in columns]
635	    column_index = {name: index for index, name in enumerate(names)}
636	    duplicate_fields = _prepare_duplicate_by(duplicate_by, names)
637	    filter_condition = _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns)

640	    decoded_pairs = []

642	    def pairs_hook(pairs):
643	        decoded_pairs.append(pairs)

647	        raise ValueError(f"constant {token} is not allowed")

650	        for row_number, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
651	            if not line.strip():
652	                continue
653	            try:
654	                decoded_pairs.clear()
655	                obj = json.loads(line, parse_constant=reject_constant, object_pairs_hook=pairs_hook)
656	            except (ValueError, RecursionError) as exc:
657	                errors.append({"row": row_number, "errors": [f"parse error: {exc}"]})
658	                continue
659	            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
660	                errors.append({"row": row_number, "errors": ["structure error: top-level value must be an object"]})
661	                continue
662	            top_keys = [key for key, _ in decoded_pairs[-1]]
663	            seen = set()
664	            duplicate = None
665	            for key in top_keys:
666	                if key in seen:
667	                    duplicate = key
668	                    break
669	                seen.add(key)
670	            if duplicate is not None:
671	                errors.append({"row": row_number, "errors": [f"structure error: duplicate key {duplicate!r}"]})
672	                continue

674	            missing = [origin for origin in sources if origin not in seen]
675	            extra = sorted(seen - expected)

678	            if extra:
679	                row_errors.append("structure error: unexpected source keys: " + ", ".join(extra))
680	            if row_errors:
681	                errors.append({"row": row_number, "errors": row_errors})
682	                continue
683	            record = {}
684	            # One slot per column keeps field errors and the lte_field
685	            # relation error attributed to a column in schema order.
686	            slots = [[] for _ in columns]
687	            field_error_names = set()
688	            for index, (column, origin) in enumerate(zip(columns, sources)):
689	                name = column["name"]
690	                converted, message = _convert_jsonl_value(column, obj[origin], defaults, markers)
691	                if message is not None:

693	                    field_error_names.add(name)

695	                enum_error = _enum_field_error(name, converted, allowed)
696	                if enum_error is not None:
697	                    slots[index].append(enum_error)
698	                    field_error_names.add(name)
699	                    continue
700	                range_error = _range_field_error(name, converted, ranges)
701	                if range_error is not None:
702	                    slots[index].append(range_error)
703	                    field_error_names.add(name)
704	                else:
705	                    record[name] = converted
706	            for name, message in _lte_field_errors(
707	                    record, field_error_names, lte_fields):
708	                slots[column_index[name]].append(message)
709	            row_errors = [message for slot in slots for message in slot]
710	            if row_errors:

721	def _csv_cell(value, quote_empty=False):
722	    """Serialize one normalized value to a single CSV cell.
723	
724	    Integers are decimal text (booleans, checked first, are lowercase
725	    ``true``/``false``), null is an empty cell, and strings keep their
726	    normalized content including any embedded CR/LF characters. The same
727	    quoting rule applies to every cell (headers included): a cell that
728	    contains a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes
729	    with each interior double quote doubled. An empty cell stays bare,
730	    except in a single-column table (``quote_empty``), where it must be a
731	    quoted empty string so the row cannot collapse into a skipped blank
732	    line; every other cell stays unquoted.
733	    """
734	    if value is None:
735	        text = ""
736	    elif isinstance(value, bool):
737	        text = "true" if value else "false"
738	    elif isinstance(value, int):
739	        text = str(value)
740	    else:
741	        text = value
742	    if text == "" and not quote_empty:
743	        return text
744	    if text == "" or any(char in text for char in (",", '"', "\r", "\n")):
745	        return '"' + text.replace('"', '""') + '"'
746	    return text

749	def _csv_payload(names, records):
750	    """Serialize the header and kept records to LF-terminated CSV text.
751	
752	    The header uses the schema output names in declared order (never
753	    ``source`` aliases); data rows follow kept-record order. The output is
754	    UTF-8 text with no BOM and every line ends in LF, including the header
755	    and the final record (an empty result still yields the header alone).
756	    """
757	    single_column = len(names) == 1
758	    lines = [",".join(_csv_cell(name, single_column) for name in names)]
759	    lines.extend(
760	        ",".join(_csv_cell(record[name], single_column) for name in names)
761	        for record in records)
762	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

765	def _stage_output(destination, payload):
766	    """Serialize payload text into a temp file in the destination's directory.
767	
768	    Parent directories are never created and the destination is not
769	    touched. Returns (staged_path, existed); raised OSError names the
770	    target path.
771	    """
772	    target = Path(destination)
773	    parent = target.parent
774	    if not parent.exists() or not parent.is_dir():
775	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: parent directory does not exist")
776	    if target.exists() and target.is_dir():
777	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: target is a directory")
778	    if target.exists() and not os.access(target, os.W_OK):
779	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: target is not writable")
780	    try:
781	        handle, staged_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
782	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent)
783	    except OSError as exc:
784	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
785	    staged = parent / staged_name
786	    try:
787	        out = os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
788	    except BaseException:
789	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
790	            os.close(handle)
791	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
792	            staged.unlink()
793	        raise
794	    try:
795	        with out:
796	            out.write(payload)
797	    except OSError as exc:
798	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
799	            staged.unlink()
800	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
801	    except BaseException:
802	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
803	            staged.unlink()
804	        raise
805	    return staged, target.exists() and not target.is_dir()

808	def _install_staged(target, staged, existed):
809	    """Replace target with staged, keeping its old bytes recoverable.
810	
811	    Returns the backup path (or None). If the swap fails after the
812	    original was moved aside, the original is restored at target before
813	    the OSError (naming target) is raised.
814	    """
815	    mode = None
816	    backup = None
817	    try:
818	        if existed:
819	            mode = target.stat().st_mode & 0o7777
820	            # Reserve a unique backup name so an unrelated user file can
821	            # never be clobbered; os.replace below overwrites the empty
822	            # placeholder with the original file.
823	            backup_handle, backup_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
824	                prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".backup", dir=target.parent)
825	            os.close(backup_handle)
826	            backup = target.parent / backup_name
827	            os.replace(target, backup)
828	        os.replace(staged, target)
829	        if mode is not None:
830	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
831	                target.chmod(mode)
832	        else:
833	            # mkstemp creates 0600; a freshly created output historically
834	            # got the usual 0666 & ~umask mode from open().
835	            umask = os.umask(0)
836	            os.umask(umask)
837	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
838	                target.chmod(0o666 & ~umask)
839	    except OSError as exc:
840	        if backup is not None:
841	            if target.exists():
842	                # The original never left target; just drop the placeholder.
843	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
844	                    backup.unlink()
845	            else:
846	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
847	                    os.replace(backup, target)
848	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
849	    return backup

852	def _write_outputs_atomic(output_path, output_payload, errors_path, errors):
853	    """Write both output files as one all-or-nothing operation.
854	
855	    Either both files are fully written (replacing existing files), or a
856	    filesystem failure leaves every target exactly as it was beforehand:
857	    pre-existing files keep their bytes and previously absent files stay
858	    absent. Parent directories are never created. The records output
859	    carries output_payload (JSONL or CSV text); the errors output is
860	    always JSONL.
861	    """
862	    errors_payload = "".join(
863	        json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
864	        for record in errors)
865	    output_target, errors_target = Path(output_path), Path(errors_path)
866	    staged_output, output_existed = _stage_output(output_target, output_payload)
867	    try:
868	        staged_errors, errors_existed = _stage_output(errors_target, errors_payload)
869	    except BaseException:
870	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
871	            staged_output.unlink()
872	        raise
873	    installs = []
874	    try:
875	        installs.append((output_target,
876	                         _install_staged(output_target, staged_output, output_existed)))
877	        installs.append((errors_target,
878	                         _install_staged(errors_target, staged_errors, errors_existed)))
879	    except BaseException:
880	        # Undo only fully completed installs; a failed _install_staged
881	        # has already restored that target itself.
882	        for target, backup in installs:
883	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
884	                if backup is not None:
885	                    os.replace(backup, target)
886	                else:
887	                    target.unlink()
888	        for leftover in (staged_errors, staged_output):
889	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
890	                leftover.unlink()
891	        raise
892	    for _, backup in installs:
893	        if backup is not None:
894	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
895	                backup.unlink()

898	def _check_path_isolation(source, schema, output, errors):
899	    """Reject when an output aliases an input or the other output.
900	
901	    Runs before either input is read or either output is written. Two
902	    paths alias when their resolved pathnames are equal (identical paths,
903	    including relative/absolute spellings and symbolic-link aliases) or,
904	    when both paths currently exist, when they share a device and inode
905	    (distinct hard links to the same file). Outputs that do not exist yet
906	    only take part in the pathname comparison, so two fresh names are not
907	    refused merely because they could later be linked together. File
908	    names, extensions and directories never decide identity, and two
909	    independent files with identical contents are always allowed. Any I/O
910	    error resolving or stating a path propagates as OSError naming it.
911	    """
912	    roles = (
913	        ("source", Path(source)),
914	        ("schema", Path(schema)),
915	        ("records output", Path(output)),
916	        ("errors output", Path(errors)),
917	    )
918	
919	    def resolve(path):
920	        try:
921	            return path.resolve()
922	        except OSError as exc:
923	            raise OSError(f"cannot check path {path}: {exc}") from None
924	
925	    def file_identity(labeled_path, resolved):
926	        try:
927	            result = resolved.stat()
928	        except FileNotFoundError:
929	            return None
930	        except OSError as exc:
931	            raise OSError(f"cannot check path {labeled_path}: {exc}") from None
932	        return result.st_dev, result.st_ino
933	
934	    entries = [(label, path, resolve(path)) for label, path in roles]
935	    # Pairs involving at least one output, in a fixed order: the two
936	    # outputs, then records output against the inputs, then errors output.
937	    pairs = ((2, 3), (2, 0), (2, 1), (3, 0), (3, 1))
938	    for left_index, right_index in pairs:
939	        left_label, left_path, left_resolved = entries[left_index]
940	        right_label, right_path, right_resolved = entries[right_index]
941	        if left_resolved == right_resolved:
942	            raise ValueError(
943	                f"paths must be distinct: {left_label} {left_path} and "
944	                f"{right_label} {right_path} point to the same file")
945	        left_identity = file_identity(left_path, left_resolved)
946	        right_identity = file_identity(right_path, right_resolved)
947	        # A not-yet-existing path (or a dangling link to one) cannot
948	        # currently be hard-linked to an existing file; the resolved
949	        # pathname comparison above still applies to both spellings.
950	        if left_identity is None or right_identity is None:
951	            continue
952	        if left_identity == right_identity:
953	            raise ValueError(
954	                f"paths must be distinct: {left_label} {left_path} and "
955	                f"{right_label} {right_path} point to the same existing file")
956

958	def main():

962	    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
963	    parser.add_argument("--errors", required=True)

966	                        help="records output format: jsonl (default) or csv")

968	                        help="output field to report duplicate accepted records by; repeatable")

970	                        help='equality condition as JSON, e.g. {"field": "active", "value": true}')

975	        # before either input is read, independently of --format: names and
976	        # extensions never decide either format.

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from data_importer import normalize_csv, normalize_jsonl, write_jsonl

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def run_cli(source, output, errors, fmt=None, extra=(), output_format=None):
    command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(source),
               "--schema", str(ROOT / "samples/schema.json"),
               "--output", str(output), "--errors", str(errors)]
    if fmt is not None:
        command += ["--format", fmt]
    if output_format is not None:
        command += ["--output-format", output_format]
    command += list(extra)
    return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)


def hidden_entries(directory):
    return [path.name for path in Path(directory).iterdir() if path.name.startswith(".")]



class ImporterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.schema = json.loads((ROOT / "samples/schema.json").read_text())

    def test_types_whitespace_and_optional_null(self):
        result = normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/customers.csv", self.schema)
        self.assertEqual(result["accepted"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["records"][0], {"name": "Maya", "orders": 3, "active": True})
        self.assertIsNone(result["records"][1]["orders"])

    def test_row_errors_preserve_valid_rows(self):
        result = normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/mixed.csv", self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 2))
        self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [3, 4])
        self.assertIn("orders", result["errors"][0]["errors"][0])

    def test_invalid_schema_and_header(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/customers.csv", {"columns": [{"name": "name", "type": "date"}]})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/customers.csv", {"columns": [{"name": "other", "type": "string"}]})

    def mapped_schema(self):
        return {"columns": [
            {"name": "name", "type": "string", "required": True, "source": "display_name"},
            {"name": "orders", "type": "integer", "source": "purchase_count"},
            {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "required": True},
        ]}

    def write_csv(self, directory, text):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def write_csv_bytes(self, directory, data):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return path

    def test_physical_rows_blank_and_multiline_fixture(self):
        text = ("name,orders,active\n\n\"Ma\nya\",3,true\nBad,x,true\n"
                "\"No\nra\",2,\nZ,3,false\n")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema, duplicate_by=["orders"])
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, 2))
        self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [5, 6])
        self.assertIn("orders", result["errors"][0]["errors"][0])
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][1]["errors"], ["active: required value is empty"])
        self.assertEqual([record["name"] for record in result["records"]], ["Ma\nya", "Z"])
        self.assertEqual(result["duplicates"],
                         [{"key": {"orders": 3}, "record_numbers": [1, 2]}])

    def test_physical_rows_line_endings_bom_and_no_final_newline(self):
        base = (b"name,orders,active\r\n\r\n\"Ma\r\nya\",3,true\r\nBad,x,true\r\n"
                b"\"No\r\nra\",2,\r\nZ,3,false\r\n")
        lone_cr = base.replace(b"\r\n", b"\r")
        bom = b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + base
        no_final = base[:-2]  # drop trailing CRLF
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for data in (base, lone_cr, bom, no_final):
                csv_path = self.write_csv_bytes(directory, data)
                result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
                self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, 2), data)
                self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [5, 6], data)

    def test_physical_rows_multiline_reject_counts_once(self):
        # A quoted field spanning lines is one record; its error reports the
        # starting physical line. Consecutive/trailing blank lines add nothing.
        text = "name,orders,active\n\n\n\"a\nb\",nope,\n\"x\n\ny\",1,true\n\n"
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 4)
        self.assertEqual([m.split(":", 1)[0] for m in result["errors"][0]["errors"]],
                         ["orders", "active"])
        self.assertEqual(result["records"][0]["name"], "x\n\ny")

    def test_physical_rows_whitespace_only_keeps_csv_rule(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\n   \n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual(result["rejected"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"], ["wrong number of cells"])

    def test_source_mapping(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "display_name,purchase_count,active\nMaya,3,TRUE\n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.mapped_schema())
            self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"name": "Maya", "orders": 3, "active": True}])
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 0))

    def test_source_swap_and_target_name_overlap(self):
        schema = {"columns": [
            {"name": "first", "type": "string", "source": "second"},
            {"name": "second", "type": "string", "source": "first"},
        ]}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "second,first\nalpha,beta\n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, schema)
            self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"first": "alpha", "second": "beta"}])

    def test_source_mapping_row_errors_and_counts(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "display_name,purchase_count,active\nMaya,3,TRUE\n,nope,TRUE\n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.mapped_schema())
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 1))
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 3)
            self.assertTrue(any("name" in error for error in result["errors"][0]["errors"]))
            self.assertTrue(any("orders" in error for error in result["errors"][0]["errors"]))

    def test_source_mapping_header_mismatch(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for header in ("name,purchase_count,active\n", "display_name,purchase_count\n",
                           "display_name,purchase_count,active,extra\n", "purchase_count,display_name,active\n"):
                csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, header)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    normalize_csv(csv_path, self.mapped_schema())

    def test_invalid_source_values(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "display_name\nMaya\n")
            for bad in (None, 3, True, "", "   ", ["display_name"]):
                schema = {"columns": [{"name": "name", "type": "string", "source": bad}]}
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                    normalize_csv(csv_path, schema)
                self.assertIn("name", str(caught.exception))

    def test_conflicting_sources(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "display_name,active\nMaya,TRUE\n")
            schema = {"columns": [
                {"name": "name", "type": "string", "source": "display_name"},
                {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "source": "display_name"},
            ]}
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                normalize_csv(csv_path, schema)
            message = str(caught.exception)
            self.assertIn("name", message)
            self.assertIn("active", message)
            self.assertIn("display_name", message)
            schema["columns"] = [
                {"name": "name", "type": "string"},
                {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "source": "name"},
            ]
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                normalize_csv(csv_path, schema)
            message = str(caught.exception)
            self.assertIn("name", message)
            self.assertIn("active", message)

    def test_cli_mapping_error_keeps_existing_output(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,TRUE\n")
            schema_path = Path(directory) / "schema.json"
            schema_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.mapped_schema()), encoding="utf-8")
            output, errors = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl", Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl"
            output.write_text("keep me\n", encoding="utf-8")
            command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(csv_path), "--schema", str(schema_path), "--output", str(output), "--errors", str(errors)]
            run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 2)
            self.assertIn("error", json.loads(run.stdout))
            self.assertEqual(output.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "keep me\n")
            self.assertFalse(errors.exists())

    def test_cli_jsonl_and_exit_status(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            output, errors = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl", Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl"
            command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(ROOT / "samples/mixed.csv"), "--schema", str(ROOT / "samples/schema.json"), "--output", str(output), "--errors", str(errors)]
            run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 1, run.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(json.loads(run.stdout), {"accepted": 1, "rejected": 2})
            self.assertEqual(len(output.read_text().splitlines()), 1)
            self.assertEqual(len(errors.read_text().splitlines()), 2)
            command[-1] = str(output)
            self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True).returncode, 2)


    def test_duplicate_report_groups_and_record_numbers(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(
                directory,
                "name,orders,active\n"
                "a,3,TRUE\n"
                "b,3,true\n"
                "bad,x,true\n"
                "c,,true\n"
                "d,,false\n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema, duplicate_by=["orders"])
            self.assertEqual(len(result["records"]), 4)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (4, 1))
            self.assertEqual(result["duplicates"], [
                {"key": {"orders": 3}, "record_numbers": [1, 2]},
                {"key": {"orders": None}, "record_numbers": [3, 4]},
            ])

    def test_duplicate_report_disabled_or_absent(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\na,3,TRUE\nb,3,true\n")
            self.assertNotIn("duplicates", normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema))
            self.assertNotIn("duplicates", normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema, None))
            unique = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\na,1,TRUE\nb,2,true\n")
            self.assertEqual(normalize_csv(unique, self.schema, duplicate_by=["orders"])["duplicates"], [])

    def test_duplicate_report_composite_and_first_seen_order(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(
                directory,
                "name,orders,active\n"
                "a,1,true\n"
                "b,2,false\n"
                "c,1,true\n"
                "d,2,true\n"
                "e,2,false\n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema, duplicate_by=["orders", "active"])
            self.assertEqual(result["duplicates"], [
                {"key": {"orders": 1, "active": True}, "record_numbers": [1, 3]},
                {"key": {"orders": 2, "active": False}, "record_numbers": [2, 5]},
            ])

    def test_duplicate_by_invalid_config_raises_before_reading(self):
        missing = ROOT / "samples" / "does-not-exist.csv"
        cases = ["orders", [], ["orders", "orders"], [""], ["  "], [3], ("orders",),
                 ["nope"], ["active", "nope"]]
        for value in cases:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                normalize_csv(missing, self.schema, duplicate_by=value)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            normalize_csv(missing, self.schema, duplicate_by=["orders", "nope"])
        self.assertIn("nope", str(caught.exception))
        # a source name is not accepted as a field name
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "display_name,purchase_count,active\nMaya,3,TRUE\n")
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                normalize_csv(csv_path, self.mapped_schema(), duplicate_by=["purchase_count"])

    def test_cli_duplicate_by_flag(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(
                directory,
                "name,orders,active\nA,3,TRUE\nB,3,true\nC,,true\nBAD,x,true\nD,,true\n")
            output, errors = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl", Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl"
            command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(csv_path),
                       "--schema", str(ROOT / "samples/schema.json"),
                       "--output", str(output), "--errors", str(errors),
                       "--duplicate-by", "orders"]
            run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 1, run.stderr)
            summary = json.loads(run.stdout)
            self.assertEqual(summary["accepted"], 4)
            self.assertEqual(summary["rejected"], 1)
            self.assertEqual(summary["duplicates"], [
                {"key": {"orders": 3}, "record_numbers": [1, 2]},
                {"key": {"orders": None}, "record_numbers": [3, 4]},
            ])
            self.assertEqual(len(output.read_text().splitlines()), 4)
            self.assertEqual(len(errors.read_text().splitlines()), 1)

    def test_cli_duplicate_by_bad_field_exit_two_keeps_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\nA,3,TRUE\n")
            schema_path = Path(directory) / "schema.json"
            schema_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.mapped_schema()), encoding="utf-8")
            output, errors = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl", Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl"
            output.write_text("keep me\n", encoding="utf-8")
            command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(csv_path),
                       "--schema", str(schema_path), "--output", str(output),
                       "--errors", str(errors), "--duplicate-by", "purchase_count"]
            run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 2)
            payload = json.loads(run.stdout)
            self.assertIn("error", payload)
            self.assertIn("purchase_count", payload["error"])
            self.assertEqual(output.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "keep me\n")
            self.assertFalse(errors.exists())

    def test_filter_eq_keeps_matches_and_counts_filtered(self):
        # Three valid rows, two match active=true; a fourth row is invalid
        # and must still reach errors with its physical line number.
        text = ("name,orders,active\n"
                "a,1,true\n"
                "b,,true\n"
                "c,3,false\n"
                "d,x,true\n")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema,
                                   filter_eq={"field": "active", "value": True})
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["filtered"], result["rejected"]), (2, 1, 1))
        self.assertEqual([record["name"] for record in result["records"]], ["a", "b"])
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 5)
        self.assertTrue(all(record["active"] is True for record in result["records"]))

    def test_filter_eq_null_matches_only_normalized_empty(self):
        text = ("name,orders,active\n"
                "a,,true\n"
                "b,0,true\n"
                "c,,false\n")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            null_result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema,
                                        filter_eq={"field": "orders", "value": None})
            zero_result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema,
                                        filter_eq={"field": "orders", "value": 0})
        self.assertEqual([r["name"] for r in null_result["records"]], ["a", "c"])
        self.assertEqual(null_result["filtered"], 1)
        self.assertEqual([r["name"] for r in zero_result["records"]], ["b"])
        self.assertEqual(zero_result["filtered"], 2)

    def test_filter_eq_string_exact_case_and_padding(self):
        text = ("name,orders,active\n"
                "Maya,1,true\n"
                "maya,2,true\n")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:

                                   filter_eq={"field": "name", "value": " Maya "})

        self.assertEqual([r["name"] for r in folded["records"]], ["maya"])
        self.assertEqual(padded["accepted"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(padded["filtered"], 2)

    def test_filter_eq_no_match_keeps_blank_line_order(self):
        text = "name,orders,active\na,1,true\n\nb,2,true\n"

        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["filtered"], result["rejected"]), (0, 2, 0))
        self.assertEqual(result["records"], [])
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"], [])

    def test_filter_eq_with_duplicate_by_renumbers_kept_records(self):

                "a,3,true\n"
                "b,3,false\n"
                "c,3,true\n"
                "bad,x,true\n"
                "d,3,true\n")

                                   filter_eq={"field": "active", "value": True})

        self.assertEqual([r["name"] for r in result["records"]], ["a", "c", "d"])
        self.assertEqual(result["duplicates"],
                         [{"key": {"orders": 3}, "record_numbers": [1, 2, 3]}])

    def test_filter_eq_disabled_or_none_unchanged(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\na,1,true\nb,2,false\n")
            omitted = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)

        self.assertEqual(omitted, explicit_none)
        self.assertEqual(set(omitted), {"records", "errors", "accepted", "rejected"})
        self.assertNotIn("filtered", omitted)

    def test_filter_eq_invalid_config_raises_before_reading(self):
        missing = ROOT / "samples" / "does-not-exist.csv"
        cases = [
            [], "x", 3, True,
            {"field": "active"},
            {"value": True},
            {},
            {"field": "active", "value": True, "extra": 1},
            {"field": 1, "value": True},
            {"field": "  ", "value": True},

            {"field": "active", "value": 1},

            {"field": "orders", "value": 1.0},
            {"field": "orders", "value": "1"},

        # source aliases are not recognized as field names

            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:

                              filter_eq={"field": "purchase_count", "value": 3})

    def test_cli_filter_eq_flag(self):

                "a,1,true\n"
                "b,,true\n"
                "c,3,false\n"

class CsvQuoteSyntaxTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """A quoted field left open at EOF or junk after a closing quote is a
    fatal parse error for the whole CSV, not silently folded into data."""

    UNTERMINATED = "unterminated"
    AFTER_CLOSE = "after closing quote"

    def setUp(self):
        self.schema = json.loads((ROOT / "samples/schema.json").read_text())

    def write_csv(self, directory, text):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def write_csv_bytes(self, directory, data):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return path

    def assert_parse_failure(self, path, start_line, reason_part):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            normalize_csv(path, self.schema)
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn("CSV parse error", message)
        self.assertIn(str(path), message)
        self.assertIn(f"record starting line {start_line}", message)
        self.assertIn(reason_part, message)
        return message

    def test_unterminated_quoted_field_at_eof(self):
        # The exact motivating input: the final quoted field never closes.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true')
            message = self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 2, self.UNTERMINATED)
            self.assertNotIn(self.AFTER_CLOSE, message)

    def test_text_after_closing_quote_is_fatal(self):
        # "Ma"ya must not collapse into the name; letters, spaces and tabs
        # right after a closing quote are all illegal.
        cases = (
            ('name,orders,active\n"Ma"ya,3,true\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\n"Ma" ya,3,true\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\n"Ma"\tya,3,true\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true"x', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true" ,\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\n"x"y,2,false\n', 3),
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for text, line in cases:
                csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
                message = self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, line, self.AFTER_CLOSE)
                self.assertNotIn(self.UNTERMINATED, message, text)

    def test_error_line_points_to_multiline_record_start(self):
        # Even though the problem is discovered on a later physical line
        # (or at EOF), the message names where the record began. Blank
        # lines and newlines inside quoted fields all occupy line numbers.
        unterminated = ("name,orders,active\n"
                        "Maya,3,true\n"
                        "\n"
                        '"a\nb",3,true\n'
                        '"x\ny,3,true')
        after_close = ("name,orders,active\n"
                       "\n\n"
                       '"a\nb",3,true\n'
                       '"x\ny"z,3,true\n')
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, unterminated)
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 6, self.UNTERMINATED)
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, after_close)
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 6, self.AFTER_CLOSE)

    def test_quote_errors_after_valid_and_ordinary_error_rows(self):
        # Earlier accepted records and ordinary row errors cannot make the
        # later quote failure a row error: the call raises, returning
        # nothing at all.
        for text in ("name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\nBad,x,true\n\"oops,3,true\n",
                     "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\nBad,x,true\n\"Ma\"ya,3,true\n"):
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
                self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 4, "quote")

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,"active')

            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,"active"x\nMaya,3,true\n')
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 1, self.AFTER_CLOSE)

    def test_line_endings_bom_and_no_final_newline(self):
        variants = (
            b'name,orders,active\r\nMaya,3,"true',
            b'name,orders,active\rMaya,3,"true',
            b'\xef\xbb\xbfname,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true',
            b'name,orders,active\r\n"Ma"ya,3,true\r\n',
            b'name,orders,active\r"Ma"ya,3,true\r',
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for data in variants:
                csv_path = self.write_csv_bytes(directory, data)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                    normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
                self.assertIn("CSV parse error", str(caught.exception), data)
            # valid quoted multiline fields under every line convention,
            # BOM and a missing final newline keep their old semantics:
            # line bytes inside a quoted field are retained verbatim.
            for data, expected_name in (
                    (b'name,orders,active\r\n"Ma\r\nya",3,true\r\n', "Ma\r\nya"),
                    (b'name,orders,active\r"Ma\rya",3,true\r', "Ma\rya"),
                    (b'\xef\xbb\xbfname,orders,active\n"Maya",3,true\n', "Maya"),
                    (b'name,orders,active\n"Maya",3,true', "Maya")):
                csv_path = self.write_csv_bytes(directory, data)
                result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
                self.assertEqual(result["accepted"], 1, data)
                self.assertEqual(result["records"][0]["name"], expected_name, data)

class JsonlImporterTests(unittest.TestCase):

    def mapped_schema(self):
        return {"columns": [
            {"name": "name", "type": "string", "required": True, "source": "display_name"},

    def test_physical_row_numbers_skip_blank_lines(self):

            self.assertEqual(result["records"][1], {"name": "Z", "orders": None, "active": True})

    def test_integer_rules(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            accepted = '{"name": "ok", "orders": %s, "active": true}'
            rejected_values = ("3.0", "1e2", "-0.5", "true", '"3.5"', '"1e2"', "[3]")
            lines = [accepted % "42", accepted % '"-8"']
            lines.extend(accepted % value for value in rejected_values)
            path = self.write_jsonl(directory, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
            result = normalize_jsonl(path, self.schema)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, len(rejected_values)))
            self.assertEqual([record["orders"] for record in result["records"]], [42, -8])
            for row in result["errors"]:

content.content:
1	# Data Importer
2	
3	Normalize a CSV file or JSONL stream to JSONL or CSV using a small explicit schema. Requires Python 3.10+; no installation dependencies.
4	
5	`python3 data_importer.py samples/customers.csv --schema samples/schema.json --output customers.jsonl --errors errors.jsonl` converts the two valid CSV rows. The input format is chosen explicitly with `--format csv` (default) or `--format jsonl`; it is never inferred from the file extension. The records output format is chosen independently with `--output-format jsonl` (default) or `--output-format csv`; it too is never inferred from the extension, and `--format` and `--output-format` may name different formats (for example JSONL input with CSV output). For JSONL input, use `python3 data_importer.py samples/customers.jsonl --schema samples/schema.json --output customers.jsonl --errors errors.jsonl --format jsonl`; add `--output-format csv` to write the normalized records as CSV instead. `samples/mixed.csv` and `samples/mixed.jsonl` each contain one accepted row and two rejected rows. Each rejected row is written separately with its physical line number (for CSV the header is line 1) and its errors; accepted rows remain available in input order.
6	
7	The records output is JSONL unless `--output-format csv` is given. JSONL output is one sorted-key object per line exactly as before. CSV output is UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, comma-delimited, and every line ends in LF — the header and every data record alike, including the last. The header names the output fields by their schema `name` in the declared order of `schema.columns`, never their `source` aliases, and follows the same quoting rule as data; data rows follow kept-record order after filtering. Cell serialization is: integers as decimal text, booleans as lowercase `true`/`false`, null as an empty cell, and strings as their normalized content with any interior newline characters retained (a CR embedded in a value stays a CR even though record terminators are LF). A cell containing a comma, a double quote, a CR or an LF is wrapped in double quotes and each interior double quote is doubled; all other cells stay unquoted. An empty cell stays bare, except in a single-column table where it is written as a quoted empty string (`""`) so the record cannot be mistaken for a skipped blank line. As long as the import does not fail outright, the header is written even when no record is kept (all records filtered out, or every row rejected); the same normalized Chinese, special-character and null samples produce byte-identical CSV whether imported from CSV or JSONL. The errors output is always JSONL, in every output format. Validation, missing-value handling, filtering, duplicate reporting, the summary fields on standard output and the exit-code meanings are unchanged by the output format. An invalid `--output-format` exits 2 after the path-isolation check but before either input file or the schema is read: standard output carries only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string contains `output-format` and the offending value verbatim (no success summary), and neither output is created or overwritten; when both `--format` and `--output-format` are invalid the output-format error is reported. The CSV records output commits together with the JSONL errors output under the existing all-or-nothing rules: a records target that is a directory, a missing or unwritable parent on either side, an unwritable target, or a write failure exits 2 with an `error` naming the failing path, pre-existing outputs keep their bytes, previously absent outputs stay absent, no directory is created, and the input and schema files are untouched.
8	
9	
10	Schema columns specify name, type (`string`, `integer`, `boolean`), optional `required`, and an optional target-typed `default` (see below). A column may also declare an optional `source`: the CSV column, or JSONL object key, it reads from, while `name` remains the output field name; omitting `source` reads the field named by `name`. An explicit `source` must be a non-empty, non-blank string, and the effective source names must be unique across columns (a source may coincide with another field's `name`, and two fields may swap sources). For CSV the header must match the effective source names and their order exactly, compared literally without trimming or case folding. For JSONL each non-empty line must hold exactly one JSON object whose key set equals the effective source set exactly (order is free, keys match literally); missing or extra keys reject the line.
11	
12	CSV text is trimmed, absent optional values become JSON null, and booleans accept true/false without case sensitivity. CSV quote syntax is checked strictly for both the header and every data record: two double quotes inside a quoted field still denote one literal double quote, and a double quote inside an unquoted field stays an ordinary character, but a quoted field that is still open when the file ends, or any character other than a comma, a line ending or the end of the file appearing immediately after a closing quote (a space or tab included), aborts the whole parse rather than being folded into the cell value. `normalize_csv` raises `ValueError` whose message contains "CSV parse error", the input path, the offending record's starting physical line and a reason distinguishing the two problems (the header starts at line 1; a data record starts on the physical line after the preceding read record ends, so blank lines and newlines inside quoted fields shift it, and an error detected only on a later line or at EOF still points at the record start); no partial result is returned. On the CLI (the default format or explicit `--format csv`) such an error exits 2 with standard output carrying only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string carries that message (no success summary), and both outputs keep their pre-run state — existing files keep their bytes, previously absent files are not created, and the input and schema are untouched — regardless of valid records or ordinary row errors read earlier. (Ordinary per-row errors — type, required, enum or cell-count problems — still leave other rows valid and exit 1; quote-syntax failures are the only CSV parse errors that abort the run.) JSONL is read as UTF-8, allowing a leading byte-order mark; blank lines are skipped while still consuming a physical line number, and an empty or all-blank file reports zero counts. Each line is parsed independently: invalid JSON, a non-object top-level value, duplicate top-level keys, and the `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` constants reject that line and later lines are still processed. String values are trimmed; trimmed-to-empty strings and JSON null follow the same required/null rule as CSV. The `string` type accepts JSON strings only; `integer` accepts non-boolean JSON integers or strings convertible under the CSV rule (fractional and exponential JSON numbers are rejected); `boolean` accepts JSON booleans or case-insensitive `true`/`false` strings. Arrays, objects and any other value never convert implicitly and are reported as field errors. Error messages distinguish parse, structure and field errors; field errors use the output field name and are collected in schema order. Output objects use sorted keys. The input is processed in memory. Outputs replace existing files but cannot alias either input or each other; this is checked before either input is read or either output is written. Identity ignores file names, extensions and directories: two paths alias when they resolve to the same pathname (identical paths, relative or absolute, including symbolic links) or, when both currently exist, when they are the same file on disk (the same device and inode, so two distinct names hard-linked to one file alias it); two independent files with identical contents are not aliases. An output that does not exist yet only takes part in the resolved-pathname comparison. An alias conflict exits 2 with standard output carrying only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string names the paths that point to the same file (no accepted/rejected summary); the source, schema and both outputs stay exactly as they were — existing files keep their bytes, hard-link relationships and symbolic links themselves are untouched, and absent outputs are not created. Parent output directories must already exist and are never created. The two outputs commit together: on a successful run both the records and errors files are fully written (serialised into temporary files in each target's own directory, then swapped into place), while a filesystem failure (a target that is a directory, a missing or unwritable parent, an unwritable target path, or a write error) leaves both targets exactly as they were beforehand — pre-existing files keep their bytes and previously absent files stay absent. CLI exit codes are 0 for no rejected rows, 1 for row errors and 2 for an invalid format or configuration (including mapping, header or key-set mismatches), unreadable input, an alias conflict, or other I/O errors (including a path that cannot be resolved or stated); in that case standard output carries only a JSON object with a non-empty `error` string naming the failing target path (no success summary) and existing output files are left untouched (and absent ones are not created).
13	
14	A column may declare an optional `default` written as a value of the target type: `string` defaults must be strings whose trimmed value is non-empty (the trimmed value is what gets emitted), `integer` defaults must be non-boolean integers, and `boolean` defaults must be booleans (`0` and `false` are valid). `null`, arrays, objects and anything else not matching the declared type — including a blank string — is a configuration error: the API raises `ValueError` (naming both `default` and the output field) before the input is read, even when no row would have needed it, and the CLI exits 2 with only a JSON `error` object on standard output, leaving both output files exactly as they were (absent ones stay absent); the caller's schema object is never mutated. When a declared default applies, a CSV cell that is empty after trimming or a JSONL value that is JSON null or trims to empty is filled with the processed default instead of following the required/null rule — `required` columns may be filled this way in both formats. A non-empty value still converts under the ordinary type rules and an illegal non-empty value is reported as a field error exactly as before; the default never masks it. Defaults do not relax structural validation: the CSV header and cell count, and the JSONL key set and duplicate-key rules are unchanged, so a missing key or cell cannot be defaulted into a valid record. The filled value is the final value used everywhere downstream, so `filter_eq` and `duplicate_by` see it (an empty cell and the input `"3"` both become integer `3` with `default: 3`, match a `filter_eq` of 3, and group together). Columns without `default` keep the previous required and empty-value behavior in full; no default statistics are added to the result and its optional keys appear only when filtering or duplication is enabled.
15	
16	A column may declare an optional `allowed_values` list restricting its legal converted values: it must be a non-empty list whose elements already have the column's target type — strings for `string` columns (kept verbatim, never trimmed or case folded), non-boolean integers for `integer` columns, booleans for `boolean` columns; `null`, arrays and objects are never valid elements, and repeated elements judged by value equality (exact string equality) make the configuration invalid. A malformed attribute (wrong type, an empty list, a wrong-typed element, or a repeat) is a configuration error: the API raises `ValueError` naming both `allowed_values` and the output field (element errors also name the offending element, and an attribute-level error names the attribute value) before the input is read, and the CLI exits 2 with only a JSON `error` object on standard output, leaving both output files exactly as they were (absent ones stay absent); the caller's schema object is never mutated. Each row is still structurally checked, type-converted and handled for empty values exactly as before; the enum match runs on the non-null result only — an optional empty value with no default still emits `null` regardless of the list, and a required empty value still reports its ordinary error. A non-empty value that fails conversion reports only the original type error (no enum error is added); a value that converts successfully but is not in the list rejects the whole row with a field error naming the output field and `allowed_values`, while later rows are still processed. Field errors from several columns are collected in schema order and physical row numbers are unchanged; enum membership never repairs a structural error (header/cell count or key-set/duplicate-key violations). A processed `default` outside `allowed_values` is the same configuration error even when no input row would use the default, so it is rejected before the input is read. Enum validation runs before `filter_eq`: an enum-invalid row always reaches `errors` and is never hidden by filtering, while `duplicate_by` still counts only the records left after filtering. With `orders` an integer column declaring `allowed_values: [0, 3]` and `default: 3`, an empty cell and the string `"3"` both become integer `3`, `0` is kept, `4` produces the enum error, and `"bad"` produces only the integer type error; the CSV and JSONL results agree on the fixed offline samples (apart from each format's own physical row numbering and pre-existing type-error wording). Columns without `allowed_values`, and older callers, behave exactly as before: no new result keys, statistics, exit-code changes, switches, files or output formats are introduced.
17	
18	`normalize_csv` and `normalize_jsonl` accept an optional `duplicate_by` keyword: a non-empty list of output field names compared across accepted records using their trimmed, type-converted values (so integer `3` matches the string `"3"`; strings stay case-sensitive; nulls match nulls). Field names match schema `name` literally, never `source`. When enabled, the result adds a `duplicates` array; omitting the option or passing `None` leaves the result unchanged. Each group appears only when a key occurs more than once, as `{"key": {field: value, ...}, "record_numbers": [1, 4, ...]}`, where record numbers are one-based positions in `records` (rejected rows and blank JSONL lines do not count), groups are ordered by first occurrence and numbers ascend within a group. No record is removed or rejected for duplication; `accepted`, `rejected` and the exit code reflect validation only. Invalid configuration (not a list, empty list, non-string or blank entries, repeats, unknown fields) raises `ValueError` naming the offending entry before the input is read. On the CLI, repeat `--duplicate-by FIELD` once per field, in order; with bad configuration the command exits 2 with a JSON `error` on standard output and creates or overwrites neither output file. The CLI summary gains `duplicates` only when the flag is present.
19	
20	Both functions also accept an optional `filter_eq` keyword holding one equality condition, `{"field": NAME, "value": VALUE}`, and the CLI accepts the same object as a JSON string via `--filter-eq` (for example `--filter-eq '{"field": "active", "value": true}'`). Every record is fully validated and converted before the filter is applied: invalid rows still enter `errors` with their physical line numbers and are never hidden by a non-matching condition, while valid records that simply fail the predicate leave `records` out and are not counted as rejected. The condition has exactly two keys, `field` and `value`; `field` matches a schema `name` literally and case-sensitively — `source` aliases are not recognized — and must be a non-blank string. `value` is never converted or trimmed and must already fit the target field type: a string for `string` columns (case-sensitive, exact), a non-boolean integer for `integer` columns, and a boolean for `boolean` columns; `null` is allowed for every type and matches only normalized empty values. When filtering is enabled the result adds `filtered` (the number of valid rows removed by the predicate) and `accepted` equals the number of kept records; kept records stay in input order and the blank-line rules are unchanged. With `duplicate_by` enabled together, duplicates are computed over the kept records only and `record_numbers` restart at 1 in kept order. If every valid row is filtered out the records export is an empty file; the exit code is still 0 without row errors and 1 with them. Omitting the option, passing `None`, or omitting the CLI flag leaves the result structure and behavior exactly as before (no `filtered` key). 28	The schema itself is structurally validated before the data file is opened, identically by `normalize_csv` and `normalize_jsonl`: it must be an object holding a non-empty `columns` list, each column must be an object carrying `name` and `type`, `name` must be a non-blank string that is used verbatim (never trimmed) and is unique case-sensitively, `type` must be one of `string`, `integer` or `boolean`, and `required` — optional, treated as false when omitted — must be a boolean when present. # Data Importer

Normalize a CSV file or JSONL stream to JSONL or CSV using a small explicit schema. Requires Python 3.10+; no installation dependencies.

`python3 data_importer.py samples/customers.csv --schema samples/schema.json --output customers.jsonl --errors errors.jsonl` converts the two valid CSV rows. The input format is chosen explicitly with `--format csv` (default) or `--format jsonl`; it is never inferred from the file extension. The records output format is chosen independently with `--output-format jsonl` (default) or `--output-format csv`; it too is never inferred from the extension, and `--format` and `--output-format` may name different formats (for example JSONL input with CSV output). For JSONL input, use `python3 data_importer.py samples/customers.jsonl --schema samples/schema.json --output customers.jsonl --errors errors.jsonl --format jsonl`; add `--output-format csv` to write the normalized records as CSV instead. `samples/mixed.csv` and `samples/mixed.jsonl` each contain one accepted row and two rejected rows. Each rejected row is written separately with its physical line number (for CSV the header is line 1) and its errors; accepted rows remain available in input order.

The records output is JSONL unless `--output-format csv` is given. JSONL output is one sorted-key object per line exactly as before. CSV output is UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, comma-delimited, and every line ends in LF — the header and every data record alike, including the last. The header names the output fields by their schema `name` in the declared order of `schema.columns`, never their `source` aliases, and follows the same quoting rule as data; data rows follow kept-record order after filtering. Cell serialization is: integers as decimal text, booleans as lowercase `true`/`false`, null as an empty cell, and strings as their normalized content with any interior newline characters retained (a CR embedded in a value stays a CR even though record terminators are LF). A cell containing a comma, a double quote, a CR or an LF is wrapped in double quotes and each interior double quote is doubled; all other cells stay unquoted. An empty cell stays bare, except in a single-column table where it is written as a quoted empty string (`""`) so the record cannot be mistaken for a skipped blank line. As long as the import does not fail outright, the header is written even when no record is kept (all records filtered out, or every row rejected); the same normalized Chinese, special-character and null samples produce byte-identical CSV whether imported from CSV or JSONL. The errors output is always JSONL, in every output format. Validation, missing-value handling, filtering, duplicate reporting, the summary fields on standard output and the exit-code meanings are unchanged by the output format. An invalid `--output-format` exits 2 after the path-isolation check but before either input file or the schema is read: standard output carries only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string contains `output-format` and the offending value verbatim (no success summary), and neither output is created or overwritten; when both `--format` and `--output-format` are invalid the output-format error is reported. For JSONL each non-empty line must hold exactly one JSON object whose key set equals the effective source set exactly (order is free, keys match literally); missing or extra keys reject the line.

With two optional integer columns `lo` and `hi` where `lo` declares `lte_field: "hi"`, the five records `(1, 3)`, `(4, 3)`, `(null, 3)`, `(2, 2)` and `("bad", 3)` (an empty CSV cell expresses null) give `accepted` 3 and `rejected` 2 in both CSV and JSONL — the first error is the relation error on `(4, 3)` and the second is the original integer type error on `("bad", 3)`, in that order. Columns without `lte_field`, older callers, `write_jsonl` and the existing export formats, exit codes, path isolation and dual-output commit behavior are unchanged: no new result keys, statistics, switches, files or output formats are introduced.

The schema itself is structurally validated before the data file is opened, identically by `normalize_csv` and `normalize_jsonl`: it must be an object holding a non-empty `columns` list, each column must be an object carrying `name` and `type`, `name` must be a non-blank string that is used verbatim (never trimmed) and is unique case-sensitively, `type` must be one of `string`, `integer` or `boolean`, and `required` — optional, treated as false when omitted — must be a boolean when present. Any violation raises `ValueError` before the input is read; the message names `schema` and the error location with one-based column numbers, names a missing `name`/`type` key, carries the offending value verbatim, and points a duplicate name at the later column. Checks run top level first, then column by column in order (column structure, name, duplicate name, type, required) and only the first problem is reported. Unknown attributes are ignored and the caller's schema object is never mutated. On the CLI such a configuration error exits 2 with standard output carrying only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string holds the message (no success summary); existing outputs keep their bytes, absent outputs stay absent, and the input and schema files are untouched — the path-alias precheck still runs first. The `source`, `default` and `allowed_values` validations described above apply after this structural check, and valid schemas behave exactly as before in both formats.

The public API is `normalize_csv(source, schema, duplicate_by=None, filter_eq=None)` and `normalize_jsonl(source, schema, duplicate_by=None, filter_eq=None)`, each returning records, errors, counts and, when enabled, duplicates. JSONL file-open failures raise `OSError` and undecodable bytes raise `UnicodeDecodeError`. CSV export is a CLI-only addition: the signatures and result structures of both normalizers, and the JSONL export behavior of `write_jsonl(path, records)`, are unchanged. `write_jsonl(path, records)` persists either sequence with deterministic serialization. Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for API conversion and CLI checks.
